value.hook: Before reviewing daemon-bounce retries or a long-lived authenticated client
value.title: Restart recovery includes credential rotation

sections.name: body
sections.value:
A refused connection proves that attempt reached no daemon. It does not prove the cached credential belongs to the daemon that returns. pij publishes a fresh daemon.key on each successful boot. Retrying an already-authenticated request can therefore turn a restart into a 401 against a healthy replacement.

Review credential lifetime with transport recovery. Refresh local boot credentials safely, but keep explicit job/source tokens distinct. Preserve the refusal-only retry rule: a reset, timeout or request that could have reached an application handler must not be blindly replayed.

The recovery test must change the replacement server's credential and validate Authorization. A server that keeps the old dummy key, or accepts any header, proves port recovery but not real daemon-bounce recovery. Pair that positive case with a request-read-once/reset control, and keep hook/registration/inbox fast paths outside tool-only backoff. Use fixture credentials, never real credential files.

Evidence: the source trace and proof boundary in reviewer output 2026-11/10-verdict-pr-219-0a693ca.dd.json; daemon auth::stage_key/publish, Rust DaemonClient::transmit, and Copilot's per-request fetch loop. This lesson is not a passed-repair receipt.
